tools.name: spawn
tools.description: Start a child session to work on part of your task in parallel. The child is a separate agent with its own git worktree and branch of this repository (in a folder that is not a git repository with a commit, it shares the folder with you and has no branch), and it does not see your conversation, so `prompt` must say everything it needs. Returns at once with the child's id and branch while the child works in the background; call wait_for to get its report. Children cannot spawn children; spawn as many as the work needs, rather than reusing a child for unrelated work. A child is archived automatically once every pull request it opened is merged and it is idle: its worktree is removed three days later, its branch kept. When this machine is too loaded for another agent, fails with `host_busy` and `retry_after_secs`: keep working or call wait_for, then retry.

model.description: Model, in the provider's own naming. Defaults to yours on your provider, otherwise to that provider's default.

permission_mode.description: What the child may do without asking; at most your own mode. Defaults to yours.

oneOf.description: Reads only; every write or command is refused.
Asks before every write or command.
Edits files freely; asks before commands.
Does anything without asking.

prompt.description: Complete instructions for the child: the goal, the files and context it needs, constraints, and what to report back when done. The child sees nothing else of your conversation.

provider.description: Vendor CLI that runs the child, e.g. "claude" or "codex"; must be one of this task's providers. Defaults to yours.

task.description: Short label for the child's work, shown to the user in the task tree, e.g. "Fix the flaky auth tests".

branch.description: Branch the child works on, in this repository; absent when this folder is not a git repository with a commit, so the child works in the folder itself, as you do.

child.description: The new child; pass it to send, status and wait_for.

tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a follow-up prompt to a child: a correction, the next step, or a reply to its report. An idle child starts its next turn on it at once; a working child gets it after its current turn ends, in the order sent, and `queued` is then true. Either way its report comes through wait_for. An archived child is unarchived first, with its worktree back on its branch. To unblock a child waiting on a question or approval, use answer instead.

child.description: The child, as returned by spawn.

text.description: The message, as a prompt to the child.

queued.description: True when the message waits behind the child's running turn; false when the child started a turn on it.

tools.name: send_session
tools.description: Send a message to another existing session on this host. Its agent receives an attributed prompt through its normal queue; no new session or automatic reply is created. Supply a stable message_id and reuse it when retrying. Cannot send to yourself, an archived/moved session, or an agent with higher permissions. Relay chains are bounded. Do not repeatedly acknowledge or bounce messages. Existing child send/status/wait_for behavior is unchanged.

message_id.description: Stable unique key for this delivery. Reuse on retries; never reuse for different text.

session_id.description: Destination session ID on this host; never your own session.

text.description: Message text. The recipient sees it as an agent message, not human instructions.

duplicate.description: True when this sender/key was already accepted; no second prompt was created.

queued.description: Whether the message was accepted behind an active turn or an existing queued prompt.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Snapshot of your children: each one's task, branch, status, latest report, and the questions and approval requests waiting for your answer. Archived children are listed too, as `archived`, with their latest report. Returns at once; use wait_for to block until something changes.

children.description: Children to report on. Defaults to all of yours.

items.description: Identifies a session; a ULID string, opaque to receivers.

children.description: One entry per child, oldest first.

branch.description: Branch the child works on, in this repository; absent when this folder is not a git repository with a commit, so the child works in the folder itself, as you do.

last_report.description: Summary of its latest finished turn; absent before the first one ends.

open_questions.description: Its questions and approval requests waiting for your answer.

items.description: A child's question or approval request that waits for an answer.

oneOf.description: The child asked a question. Answer with `question_id` and `text`, or `choice` when it lists choices.

choices.description: Answers to pick from by position; empty for a free-text answer.

oneOf.description: The child wants to run a tool call it may not run unasked. Answer with `approval_id` and `decision`.

summary.description: What the child wants to do.

status.description: `running` while it works or waits on you, `waiting_for_capacity` while its next turn waits for this machine to have room (it still counts as working), `idle` when its turn ended, `needs_you` when it waits on the user, `error` when it cannot continue, `archived` when it was archived, by herder once all its pull requests merged or by hand (send unarchives it).

oneOf.description: Waiting for a prompt.
The agent is working, or waiting for its primary session to answer an approval or question.

A prompt waits for host capacity or its reported usage reset (retry_at); the turn starts, and the
status becomes `running`, once it does. Survives a daemon restart, and the prompt keeps
its place in the host's queue.
Blocked on a user: an approval or question routed or escalated to the user, or a failed turn to act on.
Cannot continue without intervention.
Put away by a user; read-only.
Handed off to another host; read-only here.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Block until a child needs you: it finished a turn (`report`), or it asked a question or requested an approval that waits for your answer (`request`). Returns the oldest such event that no earlier wait_for returned, at once if one is already waiting; each event is returned once. Pass `child` to wait for that child only, or omit it to wait for any. Returns `timeout` when `timeout_secs` pass first, and `idle` at once when no awaited child is working and nothing waits for you. A child that completed its turn with nothing queued and every pull request it opened merged is archived by the time you get its report, with `status` `archived`; otherwise it stays `idle`. A child whose turn failed or was interrupted, or that waits on a question or approval, is never archived automatically.

child.description: Wait for this child only. Omit to wait for any of yours.

oneOf.description: A child finished a turn and is idle again, or stopped on an error.

status.description:
The child's status now: `archived` when herder archived it after this turn, as all
its pull requests are merged.

oneOf.description: Waiting for a prompt.
The agent is working, or waiting for its primary session to answer an approval or question.

A prompt waits for host capacity or its reported usage reset (retry_at); the turn starts, and the
status becomes `running`, once it does. Survives a daemon restart, and the prompt keeps
its place in the host's queue.
Blocked on a user: an approval or question routed or escalated to the user, or a failed turn to act on.
Cannot continue without intervention.
Put away by a user; read-only.
Handed off to another host; read-only here.

summary.description: The child's final message of that turn, or what went wrong.

oneOf.description: A child is blocked on a question or approval request waiting for your answer.
The child asked a question. Answer with `question_id` and `text`, or `choice` when it lists choices.

choices.description: Answers to pick from by position; empty for a free-text answer.

oneOf.description: The child wants to run a tool call it may not run unasked. Answer with `approval_id` and `decision`.

summary.description: What the child wants to do.

oneOf.description: Nothing happened within `timeout_secs`; your children are still working.

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Answer a question or approval request that a child put to you, unblocking it. Pass the `child` that asked; for a question add `question_id` with `text`, or `choice` when it lists choices; for an approval add `approval_id` with `decision`. Your answer is final and the child acts on it, so escalate instead when the decision belongs to the user. Fails with `already_resolved` when someone answered first.

approval_id.description: The approval request to decide. Pass it with `decision`.

child.description: The child whose question or approval request this is, as wait_for or status named it.

choice.description: Position of the chosen answer in the question's `choices`, from 0.

decision.description: `allow` runs the tool call once, `deny` refuses it.

oneOf.description: Run the tool call once.
Refuse the tool call.

question_id.description: The question to answer. Pass it with `text` or `choice`.

tools.name: escalate
tools.description: Hand a question or approval request that a child put to you over to the user, when the decision is theirs rather than yours: product or scope choices, credentials, anything destructive or outside the task. The child stays blocked until the user answers. Pass the `child` that asked, `question_id` or `approval_id`, and a `note` with what the user should know to decide.

approval_id.description: The approval request to hand over.

child.description: The child whose question or approval request this is, as wait_for or status named it.

note.description: What the user should know to decide: your view, the options, the risk.

tools.name: show_html
tools.description: Show a self-contained HTML page inline in this thread, where the call happens, so the user sees it rendered live. Use it when something reads better as a visual than as prose: data as a chart or table, a diagram or code map, side-by-side mocks of several UI options, or an interactive exploration. Do not use it for ordinary answers. Write one complete HTML document with all CSS, JavaScript, SVG and data inline. The page has no network: remote scripts, stylesheets, fonts and images do not load and fetches fail, so use no CDN libraries and embed the data in the page. Support light and dark with `prefers-color-scheme` (dark is the common case). Make it responsive: readable in a column about 700px wide and on a phone, with no fixed widths that overflow. Keep it under 1 MiB. `title` is a short label shown above the page. Returns at once; still write a short text reply that summarises what the page shows, adding what it does not say.

html.description: One complete, self-contained HTML document, at most 1 MiB, with all CSS, JavaScript, SVG and data inline.

title.description: Short label shown above the page, e.g. "Request latency by endpoint".

tools.name: overview
tools.description: Snapshot of the herder daemon you run in, as its apps see it: `you`, your own session's id; every session on this host with its status, title, project and queue; every project; and every account with its usage. Use it to find the ids the command tool takes. Returns at once.

accounts.description: Every account sessions may run on, with its usage.

items.description: A provider login on this host, used through its own config dir.

config_dir.description: Config directory on the host; absent for the provider default.

email.description:
Email address the provider login is signed in as, as its CLI last reported it; absent
until it reports one, and for a login without one, such as an API key. Accounts with
the same provider and email share one login, and so its limits.

label.description: Display label chosen by the owner.

usage.description: Every limit window the provider last reported; empty until it reports one.

items.description: Usage of one provider limit window, such as a five-hour or weekly limit.

resets_at.description: When the window resets; absent when the provider does not say.

used_percent.description: Share of the window's limit used, from 0 to 100.

window.description: Window name, in the provider's own naming.

projects.description: Every project with a clone on this host.

items.description: A project as one daemon sees it: its clones on that daemon's host and its settings there.

default_account.description:
Account new sessions of the project use on this host when none is chosen; absent when

default_permission_mode.description:
Permission mode new sessions of the project start in on this host when none is chosen;

anyOf.description: How much the agent may do without asking.

Asks before every write or command.

icon.description:
The project's icon, the image an owner uploaded with `set_project_icon`, else an image
file found in its clone on this host, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes as lowercase
hex; absent when it has none. It changes whenever the image does, so clients cache the
icon by it and fetch it with `get_project_icon`.

Colour drawn behind the project's icon, as `#rrggbb`; absent when none is configured,
so a transparent icon shows through to the client's own background.

icon_uploaded.description:
Whether `icon` is an uploaded image rather than one found in the clone;

name.description: Display name: the configured name, else the last segment of the id.

paths.description: Absolute paths of the project's clones on this host.

remote.description:
The `origin` remote URL of its first clone that has one, without any password in it,

remote.

setup_command.description:
Shell command run in each new worktree of the project before its session starts;
absent when none is configured.

sessions.description: Every session on this host, archived ones included.

items.description: A session as lists show it, and the seq of its latest event.

account_id.description: Account the session runs on now.

chat.description: Whether the session is a chat, about no project.

children_need_you.description: How many of this session's children are `needs_you`; 0 for a child.

host_id.description:
Host the session runs on, one of the vault's [`ServerMessage::Hosts`]; set by a vault
only, as a daemon's sessions all run on its own host.

parent.description: Primary session of the task this session is a child of; absent for a top-level session.

parent_host.description:
Host the parent runs on when it lives on another machine; absent when the parent, if

project_id.description:
Project of the session's repository, as resolved under the daemon's current config;

Prompts waiting for the running turn to end, in the order they will run; a prompt

message_id.description: Caller-chosen stable delivery key, scoped to sender and destination.

permission_ceiling.description: Maximum permissions this message may exercise, retained while queued.

Asks before every write or command.

Does anything without asking.

sender_session_id.description: Session authenticated by the caller's MCP token, never supplied by its prompt.

tools.name: command
tools.description: Run a herder command on the daemon you run in, as the herder apps do: create, prompt, rename, archive or interrupt sessions (your own included), switch a session's model, permission mode, account or provider, link pull requests, manage projects and skills, and read or change the daemon's settings. It runs as the user who started your session (for a child, your primary's), with that user's role: commands for the daemon's owners only fail with `not_allowed` for a member. Commands that open a terminal (terminals, adding or logging in accounts, installing providers) or pair a device or host are never run for an agent; ask the user to do those in a herder app. Act only on what the user asked for: these commands change the user's real sessions and settings. Call overview first for the ids. Returns the command's result.

command.description:
The herder command, as a herder app sends it: its `type` and that command's arguments
beside it, e.g. `{"type": "rename_session", "session_id": "...", "title": "..."}`. A
call with arguments missing or wrong fails with the command's JSON Schema, so to learn
a command's arguments, call it with its `type` alone.

type.description: What the command returned: `applied` when it returns nothing more, else its own result with its fields.
